summary: Adds a search filter to the users index and new update and destroy endpoints. Adds an after_save callback that sends a welcome email.

findings.title: SQL injection in user search
findings.problem: The index action interpolates params[:q] directly into the SQL text of the where clause.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated caller can inject SQL and read or alter any table, including api_token values.
findings.fix: Pass the search term as a bound parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Any user can delete any account
findings.problem: The change exempts destroy from require_admin on line 2. The destroy action then deletes any user found by params[:id].
findings.consequence: Any authenticated non-admin can delete every account, including admin accounts.
findings.fix: Remove destroy from the require_admin exception list. Alternatively, restrict destroy to the current user's own record.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.problem: The after_save callback runs on updates as well as creates. Every user update therefore sends another welcome email.
findings.consequence: Users get a duplicate welcome email each time an admin updates their record.
findings.fix: Use after_create_commit so the email goes out only once, after the record is committed.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: The repository has no test or spec directory. Nothing exercises the search filter, update, destroy or the welcome email callback.
findings.consequence: Regressions in authorization and email behaviour reach production unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add request tests for search, update and destroy, including authorization cases. Add a model test for the email callback.

dropped.reason: The update action stays behind require_admin, so only admins can reach this find. Admins are meant to manage any user.
